prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

You are reviewing layouts of one table, all rendered in a real browser with identical content, font, padding and colours; only column widths differ. You do not know who or what produced them. The first image is the content overview (every cell on one line).
Table: 服务器安全基线核查记录 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 8 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "受检服务器唯一编号" · longest unbreakable word 18px · one-line width 120px
  col 2: header "系统账户口令强度" · longest unbreakable word 14px · one-line width 107px
  col 3: header "外部网络访问开放" · longest unbreakable word 14px · one-line width 107px
  col 4: header "日志留存天数达标" · longest unbreakable word 25px · one-line width 107px
  col 5: header "漏洞补丁更新状态" · longest unbreakable word 14px · one-line width 107px
  col 6: header "高危端口关闭数量" · longest unbreakable word 14px · one-line width 107px
  col 7: header "近三十天告警次数" · longest unbreakable word 14px · one-line width 107px
  col 8: header "应急联系人确认情况" · longest unbreakable word 14px · one-line width 120px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 528px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 527px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Rate EACH layout independently: "excellent" | "good" | "acceptable" | "poor" | "bad", with a short reason that points at what you see. Then name the best layout(s) (ties allowed), say how confident you are (low/medium/high), and note anything you are unsure about.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"","why":""},"B":{"grade":"","why":""},"C":{"grade":"","why":""},"D":{"grade":"","why":""},"E":{"grade":"","why":""},"F":{"grade":"","why":""}},"best":["letter"],"confidence":"","unsure":""}

log.raw: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"good","why":"Columns are near-even, so every header wraps to a consistent three lines and the header band reads as one horizontal unit; all values (180, 365, 11) sit comfortably and rows scan cleanly. Slightly wasteful on col 1, whose IDs are two characters, but nothing breaks or crowds."},"B":{"grade":"acceptable","why":"Col 1 is given roughly a full one-line header width (~120px) so it wraps only twice, while the seven data columns are squeezed to three-line headers. Width goes where the content is smallest (two-digit IDs) and is taken from the columns that actually hold text, leaving an uneven, front-heavy rhythm."},"C":{"grade":"good","why":"Essentially the balanced even-width solution: uniform three-line headers, equal rhythm across all eight columns, no clipped values and no orphaned characters.
